candidate_relations.reason: Puffy hand syndrome is chronic secondary lymphedema caused by lymphatic damage or obstruction from repeated intravenous injections, matching the symmetric dorsal hand edema and injection history.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Etiologic and mechanistic description of puffy hand syndrome

candidate_relations.reason: The record lacks skin sclerosis and supportive serology, while the injection-associated edema pattern supports puffy hand syndrome rather than scleroderma.
Acroangiodermatitis generally has violaceous papules or plaques and characteristic vascular proliferation, which are not shown by the biopsy or examination.
Although intravenous drug use can be associated with acroangiodermatitis, the persistent symmetric edema and small-vessel ectasia without pseudo-Kaposi morphology support puffy hand syndrome instead.
The history supports an intravenous-drug-use complication, but this label does not identify the required specific endpoint of puffy hand syndrome.
Erythromelalgia is typically painful, warm, and triggered by heat or exertion; this patient's swelling was painless and unrelated to temperature changes.
There are no CREST manifestations, skin sclerosis, or supportive autoantibodies; mild muscle-enzyme elevations alone do not establish myositis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Distinct limited systemic sclerosis with inflammatory myopathy
